rows.text:
Ahead lies the final Elation. You should not arrive with regrets. Write down your unfulfilled wishes here, and entrust them to the "Myriad Wish Grove."

...

For my last livestream, I really wanted to turn off the beauty filter and let you see what I really look like. Would you still love me then? Or was it always only that perfect "her" on the screen that you cared about?

But in the end, I couldn't bring myself to break that pretty illusion. I couldn't free myself from the person withering away behind that digital mask.

But "she" will never be me. Not now, not ever.

You can all fawn over "her" for all I care. I'm leaving.
— Kirilo, lightpaw


Eluric is a young ploo scholar of tremendous potential, a genius, even. They took just one night to completely dismantle the "Wishpower Resonance Theory" I'd spent my entire life painstakingly building. And the proof? Elegant and devastatingly simple.

It's a good thing when old dogma becomes obsolete, but my brain's already crammed with too much faulty knowledge to start my research from scratch.

May those who come after steer clear of the dead ends I've mapped out, and unlock the mystery of Wishpower sooner.
— Eiso, ploo


Why can mechatrons swap out bodies of any size so easily, while no matter how hard I train, I can never bulk up? If everything about us imagenae is predetermined from birth, do I really have the freedom to choose how I live?

Even an orch's strength has its limits! May there be no bodybuilding competitions in the World in Canvas.
— Fenrir, orch


The birthplace of emotis, the rooftop of Pearluxe Tower, the far side of the Phantasmoon, and the boundless sea of stars... There are just way too many places I want to visit. I can't even list them all! The universe is so vast, maybe the only way to make that dream of roaming the cosmos come true is to board the legendary Astral Express, huh?

I wonder... would the Nameless accept a rabbit as their traveling companion?
— Naia, moonlull


I've fulfilled the wish of Orlando the human. As for me, I only wish I had never come to this world.
— Orlando, ghost
